Controlled native CI isolated a pressure-specific append fallback: after 56 real raw-owner victims, a 173-byte strict suffix incurred 5000 source bytes and a full 4872-byte lowering despite surviving compact Index facts. Semantic coverage, current fact keys, unchanged other 62 sources, and conservation assertions passed before the final cost assertion. This proves the controlled algorithmic defect, not historical production cap crossing or continuous physical IO.

Production candidate is frozen at tree d08a358b9e1d42304188feff28d3d31648e383e6 on base84fb2559a39e9e81fd158c3e38494e2d88c35da9. Manifest compact-codex-index-provenance-source-input.json SHA d79e260f8f541473a31ae3e1c2b77eeac5344937e8cd21b086f044b9cd5aad01 binds eight postimages. Existing facts owner holds accounted compact append provenance; raw limits stay unchanged. Existing six counterfactual fixtures are byte-identical; four result-semantic, lifetime, cancellation and refusal controls are added. Independent source/accounting review is active before full normal CI. No production merge, SDK release, consumer adoption or repaired affected-case PASS yet.

Capt14/SDK30 matching adoption and bounded33-source correctness are separately complete; graph-query repair criteria remain open.
